### load data

```{r load  data, echo=FALSE}

# load the raw data, just the counts of dead individuals each day
df_raw       <- readxl::read_excel("../../Data/Summer_2026/Priming_Survival_metadata.xlsx") %>% 
                    dplyr::mutate(Family_num = as.integer(gsub("[^0-9]", "", Family)))

```

* summary stats
```{r 1 week test data summary stats}

df_raw_test <- df_raw %>% 
                    dplyr::group_by(Treatment, Family_num,  Days_Alive, Status) %>% 
                    dplyr::summarise(Deaths = dplyr::n())


append.df <- data.frame( # data frame with Days 0-7 and NA for PercSurv, use to append in the loop
  Days = c(0, 0.0833, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7),
  PercSurv = NA_real_
)


loop_t <- as.data.frame(unique(df_raw_test$Treatment))
loop_f <- as.data.frame(unique(df_raw_test$Family_num))

output.df <- data.frame()
running.df           <- data.frame(matrix(nrow = 1, ncol = 7)) # create dataframe to save cumunalitively during for loop
colnames(running.df) <- c('Family_num', 'Treatment', 'Days_Alive', 'Status', 'Deaths', 'Cumulative_deaths', 'PercSurv') # names for columns in the for loop

for (t in 1:nrow(loop_t)) {
loop_t_df <- df_raw_test %>% dplyr::filter(Treatment %in% loop_t[t,])

        for (f in 1:nrow(loop_f)) {
        loop_f.df <- loop_t_df %>% dplyr::filter(Family_num %in% loop_f[f,]) %>% dplyr::arrange(Days_Alive)
      
      
      
        loop_f.df$Cumulative_deaths <- cumsum(
          ifelse(loop_f.df$Status == 1, loop_f.df$Deaths, 0)
        )
        
        
        calc.df  <- loop_f.df %>% 
                              dplyr::mutate(
                                 PercSurv = signif( (((12-Cumulative_deaths)/12)*100), 3)
                              ) %>% 
                              dplyr::select(Family_num, Treatment, Days_Alive, Status, Deaths, Cumulative_deaths, PercSurv) %>% 
                              dplyr::rename(Days = Days_Alive)
        
        calc.df.clean <- calc.df %>%
                          dplyr::mutate(Days = signif(Days, 3)) %>% 
                          bind_rows(append.df %>% anti_join(calc.df, by = "Days")) %>% # add days that are missing, fill with NAs for other columns
                          dplyr::arrange(Days) %>% # sort by day
                          dplyr::mutate(Family_num = loop_f[f,],# fill the NAs
                                        Treatment = loop_t[t,], # fill the NAs 
                                        PercSurv = case_when(
                                          Days == 0 ~ 100, # insert 100 percent survival at time 0
                                          TRUE ~ PercSurv)) 
        
        calc.df.clean$PercSurv <- zoo::na.locf( # fille in NAs for PercSurv with the last value when no morts recorded
                                            calc.df.clean$PercSurv,
                                            na.rm = FALSE
                                          )
        
        running.df <- calc.df.clean %>% distinct(Days, PercSurv, .keep_all = TRUE)
          
 
        output.df <- rbind(output.df,
                           running.df)

        } # loop f for Family_num

} # loop t for treatment

# View(df_1week_complete)

# ascenarios at which there were morts on day 7 keep status ==1, otherwise keep the NA and 0 statu sfor 7 
# also add add EBV information
output.df <- (output.df %>%
                group_by(Treatment, Family_num, Days) %>%
                filter(
                  Days != 7 |
                  n() == 1 |
                  Status == 1 |
                  is.na(Status)
                ) %>%
                ungroup()) %>% 
                dplyr::mutate(Family_EBV = dplyr::case_when(Family_num > 45 ~ 'Low',
                                                            Family_num < 45 ~ 'High'))


SummaryStats.Treatment <- summarySE(output.df , measurevar="PercSurv", groupvars=c("Treatment", "Days")) %>%
                    dplyr::mutate(Treatment_asnum = as.numeric(substr(Treatment,1,1)),
                                  Percent_Survival =
                                    case_when(PercSurv < 0 ~ 0,
                                              TRUE ~ PercSurv),
                                  se =
                                    case_when(PercSurv < 0 ~ 0,
                                              TRUE ~ se),
                                  sd =
                                    case_when(PercSurv < 0 ~ 0,
                                              TRUE ~ sd))


SummaryStats.Treatment_EBV <- summarySE(output.df , measurevar="PercSurv", groupvars=c("Treatment","Family_EBV", "Days")) %>%
                    dplyr::mutate(Treatment_asnum = as.numeric(substr(Treatment,1,1)),
                                  Percent_Survival =
                                                case_when(PercSurv < 0 ~ 0,
                                                          TRUE ~ PercSurv),
                                              se =
                                                case_when(PercSurv < 0 ~ 0,
                                                          TRUE ~ se),
                                              sd =
                                                case_when(PercSurv < 0 ~ 0,
                                                          TRUE ~ sd))

SummaryStats.Treatment
SummaryStats.Treatment_EBV

```


```{r convert to binary}

alive_dead.df <- output.df  %>%
                                mutate(
                                  n_initial = 12, # all families started with 12 animals, 1 per tan kfor 12 tanks per treatment
                                  Cumulative_deaths = if_else(
                                    PercSurv == 100.00,
                                    0,
                                    Cumulative_deaths
                                  )
                                ) %>%
                                tidyr::fill(Cumulative_deaths, .direction = "down") %>% # fill all rows that are NA (no deaths at a given date) with the curretn deaths
                                dplyr::group_by(Family_num, Treatment) %>%
                                dplyr::arrange(Days, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
                                dplyr::mutate(
                                  new_dead = Cumulative_deaths - lag(Cumulative_deaths, default = 0),
                                  alive_after = n_initial - Cumulative_deaths) %>%
                                ungroup()

death_rows <- alive_dead.df %>%
                            filter(new_dead > 0) %>%
                            uncount(new_dead, .id = "death_number") %>%
                            mutate(
                              individual = paste(Family_num, Treatment, "dead",death_number, sep = "_"),
                              time = Days,
                              status = 1L
                            ) %>%
                            select(Treatment, Family_num, Family_EBV, individual, time, status)

censored_rows <- alive_dead.df %>%
                            group_by(Family_num, Treatment) %>%
                            slice_tail(n = 1) %>%
                            uncount(alive_after, .id = "alive_number") %>%
                            mutate(
                              individual = paste(Family_num, Treatment, "alive", alive_number, sep = "_"),
                              time = Days,
                              status = 0L
                            ) %>%
                            select(Treatment, Family_num, Family_EBV, individual, time, status)

survival_binary <- bind_rows(death_rows, censored_rows) %>%
                          arrange(Treatment, Family_num, Family_EBV, time, desc(status))


```

### create surv objects

```{r create surv objects}

surv_all <- survfit2(Surv(time, status) ~ Treatment, data = (survival_binary))

surv_HighEBV <- survfit2(Surv(time, status) ~ Treatment, data = (survival_binary %>% dplyr::filter(Family_EBV %in% 'High')))

surv_LowEBV <- survfit2(Surv(time, status) ~ Treatment, data = (survival_binary %>% dplyr::filter(Family_EBV %in% 'Low')))

```

### run cox proportional hazards 

  * run the following models 
    * surv_all - all EBV gouuops and all priming treatments 
    * surv_HighWBV and surv_LowEBV - subgroups
```{r all data cox proportional hazards model}

# prepare data column by combining the EBV group and prie treamtent to a single variable
# Why? otherwise the cox comapres to prime treamtnet 0 that is nested, making results unclear
survival_binary <- survival_binary %>% mutate(GroupEBV_PrimeTreatment = paste0(Family_EBV,"_",Treatment))

# run cox test on all data on the effect GroupEBV_PrimeTreatment
coxph.all   <- coxph(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ GroupEBV_PrimeTreatment, data = (survival_binary))
summary(coxph.all)
# GroupEBV_PrimeTreatmentHigh_1 day -0.22033   0.80226  0.17799 -1.238   0.2158    
# GroupEBV_PrimeTreatmentHigh_3 day -1.48627   0.22621  0.21432 -6.935 4.07e-12 ***
# GroupEBV_PrimeTreatmentHigh_7 day -3.65737   0.02580  0.46615 -7.846 4.30e-15 ***
# GroupEBV_PrimeTreatmentLow_0 day  -0.37665   0.68615  0.17574 -2.143   0.0321 *  
# GroupEBV_PrimeTreatmentLow_1 day  -0.17068   0.84309  0.17881 -0.955   0.3398    
# GroupEBV_PrimeTreatmentLow_3 day  -1.53459   0.21554  0.21431 -7.161 8.02e-13 ***
# GroupEBV_PrimeTreatmentLow_7 day  -3.16199   0.04234  0.37716 -8.384  < 2e-16 ***

# pot results
coxph.all_hr <- broom::tidy(coxph.all, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE)

ggplot(coxph.all_hr, aes(x = estimate, y = term)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = conf.low, xmax = conf.high), height = 0.2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = 2) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(x = "Hazard ratio", y = NULL)

coxph.all_plot <- ggforest(coxph.all, data = survival_binary)

# Note: our design is great here becuase we do not require a random factor to test thi
# each tank had a single indicidual so our survival assemssntfor family (replicates of the EBV gorup
# does not have to include a random variable in our model


pdf("../../Output/Summer_2026/survival/survival_CoxProprtionalHazards.pdf", width=8, height=5)
print(coxph.all_plot)
dev.off()


```

### Heatmap 
```{r heatmap}


# Install / load required packages
if (!requireNamespace("ggplot2",   quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("ggplot2")
if (!requireNamespace("dplyr",     quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("dplyr")
if (!requireNamespace("tidyr",     quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("tidyr")
if (!requireNamespace("grid",      quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("grid")
if (!requireNamespace("gtable",    quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("gtable")
if (!requireNamespace("scales",    quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("scales")

library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(grid)
library(gtable)
library(scales)


# ─── 3. Palette & Theme ───────────────────────────────────────

palette_low  <- "grey50"   # deep navy
palette_mid  <- "grey75"   # near-white
palette_high <- "grey95"   # deep crimson

group_bar_cols <- c("Group 1" = "#2E86AB", "Group 2" = "#E07B39")

base_family <- "sans"

theme_heatmap <- theme_minimal(base_family = base_family) +
  theme(
    # Axes
    axis.text.x  = element_text(size = 9,  angle = 35, hjust = 1, colour = "#333333"),
    axis.text.y  = element_text(size = 10, colour = "#333333", face = "bold"),
    axis.title   = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks   = element_blank(),

    # Grid
    panel.grid   = element_blank(),

    # Legend
    legend.position    = "right",
    legend.title       = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold"),
    legend.text        = element_text(size = 8),
    legend.key.width   = unit(0.5, "cm"),
    legend.key.height  = unit(1.8, "cm"),

    # Strip (group labels)
    strip.text         = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold", colour = "white"),
    strip.background   = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = NA),

    # Titles
    plot.title         = element_text(size = 15, face = "bold",   hjust = 0,
                                      colour = "#1A1A2E", margin = margin(b = 4)),
    plot.subtitle      = element_text(size = 10, colour = "#555555", hjust = 0,
                                      margin = margin(b = 16)),
    plot.caption       = element_text(size = 8,  colour = "#888888", hjust = 1),
    plot.margin        = margin(t = 16, r = 16, b = 16, l = 16),
    plot.background    = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
    panel.background   = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA)
  )

# ─── 4. Build the Heatmap ─────────────────────────────────────

ggplot( (output.df %>% dplyr::filter(Days == 7)), 
            aes(x = as.factor(Family_num), 
                y = Treatment, 
                group =Family_EBV,
                fill = PercSurv)) +

  # Tiles
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.8) +

  # Value labels inside each cell
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f", PercSurv)),
            size = 3.2, colour = "grey20", fontface = "bold") +

  # Colour scale
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low      = palette_low,
    mid      = palette_mid,
    high     = palette_high,
    midpoint = 50,
    limits   = c(0, 100),
    name     = "Score",
    labels   = label_number(suffix = "")
  ) +theme_heatmap 
  



```


# MEANse survival survival plot
```{r 1 week plot survival mean SE}
# plot relative to stocking density aas embryos 


SummaryStats.Treatment_EBV$Family_EBV <- forcats::fct_relevel(as.factor(SummaryStats.Treatment_EBV$Family_EBV), 
                                                              "Low", "High")
# plot relative to 100$% restart at D stage 
PlotMeanSE <-  ggplot(SummaryStats.Treatment_EBV, 
                      aes(x=Days, y=Percent_Survival, color=Treatment)) + geom_line()+
                          geom_point(position=position_dodge(.1))+ 
                           geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=Percent_Survival-se, 
                                             ymax=Percent_Survival+se), width=.2,
                                        position=position_dodge(.1)) +
                          scale_color_manual(values = c("darkgreen","orange","darkorange2","darkred")) +
                          theme(legend.position="right", legend.direction="vertical", 
                                legend.title = element_blank())+ theme_bw() + 
                          labs(x="Day", y="Percent Survival")+ #scale_y_continuous(breaks=seq(0,100,20))+ 
                          ggtitle("") + 
                          theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(), 
                                panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), 
                                panel.background = element_blank(), 
                                axis.line = element_line(colour = "black")) +
                          theme_classic() +
                          facet_wrap(~Family_EBV)
                    
PlotMeanSE


# output the data !!
write.csv(SummaryStats.Treatment_EBV,"../../Output/Summer_2026/survival/survival_MeanSE.csv")

pdf("../../Output/Summer_2026/survival/survival_MeanSE.pdf", width=10, height=5)
print(PlotMeanSE)
dev.off()


```

# 1 day post challenge  :::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::
ANOVA_day1 <- aov(
                  lm(Percent_Survival ~ Prime_treatment, data = (df_1week_complete %>% dplyr::filter(Date %in% 20251011)) )
                 )
shapiro.test(resid(ANOVA_day1)) # 0.09153
leveneTest(ANOVA_day1) # 0.5948
summary(ANOVA_day1) # NS 0.594

summary(BINOM_day1)

### Test data, Kaplan Meier

#### About:

* We will use the {ggsurvfit} package to generate Kaplan-Meier plots. This package aims to ease plotting of time-to-event endpoints using the power of the {ggplot2} package. See http://www.danieldsjoberg.com/ggsurvfit/index.html for details.

#### Build 'surv' object for statistical analysis 

* useful links [https://www.emilyzabor.com/tutorials/survival_analysis_in_r_tutorial.html#Comparing_survival_times_between_groups]

* What the hell does a surv object mean?? 
  
  - a 'surv' object reads ALL events as that of a dead (1) or alive (0) individual
  
  - but but but... we have volumetric count data of live and dead! Does this not throw a wrench into this type of analysis? 
  
    - Nope! Below we use logic to create a GIGANTIC table formatted correctly for this purpose!

### Test data, plot Kapla Meier

```{r 1 week plot Kaplan Meier}

km_fit <- survfit2(Surv(Days_Alive, Status) ~ Treatment, data = df_raw)

km_fit_LowEBV <- survfit2(Surv(Days_Alive, Status) ~ Treatment, data = (df_raw %>% filter(Family_num > 35)))
km_fit_HighEBV <- survfit2(Surv(Days_Alive, Status) ~ Treatment, data = (df_raw %>% filter(Family_num < 35)))


KaplanMeier.plot <- km_fit_LowEBV %>% 
                        ggsurvfit(linetype_aes = F, linewidth = 1,type ="survival") +
                        scale_color_manual(values = c("darkgreen","orange","darkorange2","darkred")) +
                        scale_fill_manual(values = c("darkgreen","orange","darkorange2","darkred")) +
                        labs(
                          x = "Days",
                          y = "Overall survival probability"
                        ) +
                        add_confidence_interval() +
                        # add_risktable() +
                        # add_risktable_strata_symbol() + # (symbol = "\U25CF", size = 10
                        scale_ggsurvfit(x_scales = list(breaks = 0:10)) +
                        add_pvalue(location  = "annotation", x = 3.5)

km_fit <- survfit(Surv(Days_Alive, Status) ~ Treatment + Family, data = df_raw)

ggsurvplot_facet(
  km_fit,
  data         = df_raw,
  facet.by     = "Family",
  color        = "Family",
  pval         = TRUE,
  conf.int     = TRUE,
  legend.title = "Family"
)

KM_hormetic_curves <- ggpubr::ggarrange(KaplanMeier.plot,
                                            hormetic_curve_MeanSE,
                                            ncol=1,
                                            nrow = 2)


# plot the surv data
pdf("../Output/Fall_2025/survival/survival_1weekrecovery_KaplanMeier.pdf", width=6, height = 8)
KM_hormetic_curves
dev.off()

# output curve 

pdf("../Output/Fall_2025/survival/survival_1weekrecovery_hormesis.pdf", width=8, height=5)
print(hormetic_curve_MeanSE)
dev.off()


fit <- coxph(Surv(Days_Alive, Status) ~ Treatment, data =  df_raw)
summary(fit)
hr <- broom::tidy(fit, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE)

ggplot(hr, aes(x = estimate, y = term)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = conf.low, xmax = conf.high), height = 0.2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = 2) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(x = "Hazard ratio", y = NULL)

```

                        # add_risktable() +

                        scale_ggsurvfit(x_scales = list(breaks = 0:10)) +
                        add_pvalue(location  = "annotation", x = 3.5)


KM_hormetic_curves <- ggpubr::ggarrange(KaplanMeier.plot,
                                            hormetic_curve_3wks_MeanSE,
                                            ncol=1,
                                            nrow = 2)


# plot the surv data
pdf("../Output/Fall_2025/survival/survival_3weeksrecovery_KaplanMeier.pdf", width=6, height = 8)
KM_hormetic_curves
dev.off()

# output curve 

pdf("../Output/Fall_2025/survival/survival_3weeksrecovery_hormesis.pdf", width=8, height=5)
print(hormetic_curve_MeanSE)
dev.off()


fit <- coxph(Surv(Days, event) ~ Prime_treatment, data =  (df_surv_3wk_expanded %>%  dplyr::filter(!Days >5)))
summary(fit)
hr <- broom::tidy(fit, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE)

ggplot(hr, aes(x = estimate, y = term)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = conf.low, xmax = conf.high), height = 0.2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = 2) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(x = "Hazard ratio", y = NULL)
